judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 2 Content Standards (same statement-type grain, identical Grade rank 1) within Strand 5 'Using Writing Conventions/Grammar Usage', but in different sub-strands: B2.5.2.1 'Apply knowledge of punctuation in written communication' (Sub-Strand 2: Using Punctuation) and B2.5.9.1 'Understand simple sentences in writing' (Sub-Strand 9: Using Simple and Compound Sentences). The source context shows substantive coherence: the punctuation standard's indicator concerns full stops at the end of sentences and question marks at the end of questions, while the sentence standard concerns identifying the structure of simple sentences — sentence boundary marking and simple-sentence structure mutually reinforce each other in written composition. This is complementary reinforcement within one writing-conventions strand rather than a demonstrated dependency, and at equal grade rank neither text supplies substantive evidence that one must precede or enable the other, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment rather than a directional buildsTowards. Shared Strand/Grade ancestry, adjacent code prefix (b2.5) and trivial token/trigram overlap ('in', 'writ-') were treated as nomination signals only.
